name: Allegheny County Courthouse and Jail

dates.altered: The data form: 'Courthouse: In 1912-14, Alden & Harlow designed stairs to main entrance; these were removed in 1928 when the street was widened. The necessary changes to the main entrance altered its proportions. In 1903-1905, F. J. Osterling enlarged the jail.'
dates.note: The HABS architectural data form gives 'DATE OF CONSTRUCTION (INCLUDE SOURCE) 1884-1886'. The style node's exemplar gives 1888 and says 1884-88, completed after Richardson's death in 1886. The two do not agree about the end date and neither is edited.

quotes.text: Courthouse & Jail connected by enclosed arched bridge. Courthouse: approx. 10-story tower on Grant Street facade; smaller towers rise from corners of interior court; heavy round-arched openings; rounded and square projections; ornate dormers. Jail: Corbeled round, square & octagonal towers; large enclosing wall.

note: Written 5 Sep 2026 for WP-11.3, Tranche 2. The survey is an NPS Form 10-920 architectural data form -- one page of field answers, not the Part I/Part II outline -- so it gives storeys, plan shape, material and alterations and NO linear dimension at all. Two things worth carrying. The stone is named as 'Pinkish-grey Milford granite', the same quarry the Trinity Church survey names for its walls, which ties the style's two most-cited buildings to one source of stone. And the form is the only place in this cluster where a surveyor writes the style's own name back at it: 'what would cone to be known as the "Richardsonian Romanesque Style."'
